maria_g: Heads-up — just finished int4 + prefetch onboarding for hypatia-15b on canary pool. Seeing intermittent OOMs on long chat sessions ( > 1200 tokens ).
ajay_k: thanks. how frequent?
maria_g: about 1-2% of requests in canary, almost always when user max_new_tokens >= 1024 and with multi-turn context.
sam_l: any memfrag traces?
maria_g: attached logs snippet in the canary run, but tl;dr heap climbs then cudaOOM during kv_alloc.

maria_g: example error: ``CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2 GiB for KV``, followed by runtime fallback to smaller batch but request still fails.

lucy: similar pattern we saw on novan-27b but that was resolved with soft-eviction + prefix-kv-prewarm.
ajay_k: did you try lowering prefetch slots or disabling prefetch entirely?
maria_g: yes — disabling prefetch reduces OOMs to practically 0 for same load, but latency regresses 15-25% p95 so not great.
sam_l: what's the default prefetch window?
maria_g: prefetch_window = 256 tokens, prefetch_stride = 128; we tried shrinking window to 128 and that cut OOMs by ~60% and p95 by ~8%.

ajay_k: interesting. maybe it's kv-slot fragmentation — int4 reduces model weights but kv allocations still align to slot boundaries causing fragmentation.
lucy: we could try the defrag + conservative-cwnd approach: run a compaction pass every N requests on idle GPU and shrink slot-reserve for canary.

maria_g: proposed plan:
- Short-term: set canary defaults -> max_new_tokens = 768 for hypatia:canary, prefetch_window = 128.
- Medium-term: enable kv-compactor at low priority (compaction_interval=30s) + soft-evict of stale prefix keys.
- Long-term: roll quant kernel update that uses compact aligned allocations for int4 (patch from runtime team).

sam_l: +1. can you post the perf numbers from the 2-run A/B?
maria_g: A (prefetch 256, max_new 1024): OOMs 1.8%, p95 latency 280ms, cost per tok baseline. B (prefetch 128, max_new 768): OOMs 0.7%, p95 256ms, token throughput -3%.
ajay_k: tradeoff looks reasonable for canary. we should gate for quality regressions — any generation diffs?
maria_g: slight increase in repetition on a handful of prompts when max_new_tokens truncated; quality team checked 50 eval prompts, no major regressions, just expected truncation artifacts on long summarization prompts.
lucy: for rollout, suggest a phased increase in max_new_tokens with soft-thresholding: reqs over 768 return a warning header and route to a heavy-tier node with more memory (dedicated).

ajay_k: config snippet for canary (proposed):
```
model_defaults: {
  max_new_tokens: 768,
  prefetch: {
    enabled: true,
    window: 128,
    stride: 128
  },
  kv_compactor: {
    enabled: true,
    interval_seconds: 30,
    aggressive: false
  }
}
```

sam_l: small suggestion: add a per-request soft_kv_limit that signals runtime to evict oldest prefix keys when allocations exceed threshold. reduces hard OOMs.
maria_g: implemented a prototype: ``soft_kv_limit=0.85 * gpu_slot_capacity``. In canary run, hard OOMs went from 1.8% -> 0.3% with minor extra latency spikes during evict windows.
lucy: sounds good. what's the rollout checklist?

maria_g: rollout checklist:
- [ ] Merge canary defaults
- [ ] Enable kv_compactor on canary nodes (low priority)
- [ ] Add request header warning for >768 tokens
- [ ] Monitor p95, OOMs, and gen-quality regressions for 48h
- [ ] If stable, bump canary capacity and test 95th percentile load

ajay_k: also add perf-bucketed SLO dashboards for hypatia:canary (latency, oom-rate, tokens/sec) and eval hooks to run 200 prompt regression nightly.
maria_g: will add dashboards and the nightly eval.

deploy-bot: Deploy plan recorded: canary defaults patch #4213 scheduled for 02:00 UTC.
sam_l: tiny nit — include a test that spins a synthetic job with multi-turn > 1500 tokens to verify eviction behavior pre-merge.
maria_g: on it. i ran a quick synthetic and saw 0 hard OOMs with soft_kv_limit set; i'll add the integration test soon.

lucy: ok let's proceed with the config changes. thanks team :thumbsup: :rocket:
ajay_k: love it. keep me posted if we still see any residual OOMs after compactor warmup.
maria_g: will follow up with the 48h results in this thread. :eyes:
